chunks.text:
What Graduation Plans are available?

Texas Tech K-12 provides the Foundation Graduation Plan with various endorsement options, allowing students to customize their education based on career interests. The Foundation Plan with Endorsement path offers a well-rounded education, enabling students to graduate with the Distinguished Level of Achievement, which can qualify them for automatic admissions to Texas public universities. Endorsements include:

Step 1: Arts & Humanities

Step 2: Business & Industry

Step 3: Multidisciplinary Studies

Step 4: STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math)

Step 5: Public Services

Each endorsement requires specific advanced coursework in addition to the Foundation Plan core courses, offering students targeted electives and opportunities to develop specialized skills.

Distinguished Level of Achievement

All students graduating from Texas Tech High School on the Foundation with Endorsement Graduation Plan will also earn the Distinguished Level of Achievement. This achievement allows you to compete for the top ten percent admissions at any Texas public university and positions you to be among those first in line for a TEXAS Grant (opens in new tab), should you qualify financially.

Link for "TEXAS Grant (opens in new tab)": http://www.collegeforalltexans.com/apps/financialaid/tofa2.cfm?ID=458

Step 1: Students admitted to Texas Tech High School as ninth graders will automatically be scheduled in courses to meet the Distinguished Level of Achievement.

Step 2: More information on current Texas graduation requirements can be found on the Texas Education Agency (TEA) website (opens in new tab)

Link for "Texas Education Agency (TEA) website (opens in new tab)": https://tea.texas.gov/academics/graduation-information/state-graduation-requirements

Endorsements

Endorsements consist of a related series of courses that provide students with in-depth knowledge of a subject area. Read more information about endorsement choices at the Texas Education Agency Graduation Toolkit (opens in new tab)

Link for "Texas Education Agency Graduation Toolkit (opens in new tab)": https://tea.texas.gov/about-tea/news-and-multimedia/brochures/tea-brochures

Step 1: In addition to the 22 credits earned on the Foundation Plan, college-bound students in Texas Tech High School will complete one advanced course credit in math and science and two credits of targeted electives.

Step 2: Each endorsement option offered by Texas Tech K-12 has one to four required electives to meet the endorsement: Currently, Texas Tech K-12 offers the endorsements in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math, business and industry, arts and humanities, and multidisciplinary studies. Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will guide you through the endorsement selection process and help you choose an endorsement that best fits your interests and existing credits. You may change your endorsement at any time prior to graduation; however, you should be aware that changes to your endorsement could result in additional required course. See the Personal Graduation Plan Checklist (opens in new tab) for specific courses required for each endorsement.

Link for "Personal Graduation Plan Checklist (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/pdf/personal-graduation-plan-checklist.pdf

Step 3: All ninth and 10th graders must select an endorsement. After 10th grade, you may opt for the Foundation Plan only with parental consent.

Please contact a Texas Tech K-12 senior academic advisor via our Support Portal (opens in new tab) for information on graduation plans. For additional graduation requirements, refer to the section on State and National Assessments (opens in a new tab).

Graduation

For our Full-Time students, the graduation tab will show which endorsement your student has selected, along with their State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) and End of Course (EOC) Mastery scores.

Graduation Requirements for Texas Tech High School Students

As a student enrolled in Texas Tech High School, you have several options for earning a high school diploma, depending on the date of your enrollment in ninth grade:

Step 1: Students enrolled in ninth grade before the 2014-15 school year must complete the Recommended High School Program (RHSP) or the Minimum High School Program (MHSP) and meet state testing requirements for your graduation plan. In some cases, you may be permitted to graduate on the Foundation Graduation Plan or the Foundation with Endorsement Graduation Plan and earn a Distinguished Level of Achievement.

Step 2: Students enrolled in ninth grade during or after the 2014-15 school year must complete the Foundation Graduation Plan plus Endorsement.

Step 3: For complete information regarding Texas graduation requirements, refer to the graduation section of the Texas Education Agency website (opens in new tab)

Link for "graduation section of the Texas Education Agency website (opens in new tab)": https://tea.texas.gov/academics/graduation-information/state-graduation-requirements

Commencement

Texas Tech K-12 celebrates eligible graduates through an annual commencement ceremony.

Ceremony dates, location, participation information, deadlines and other graduation details are published on the Texas Tech K-12 Graduation & Scholarships webpage.

Link for "Tech K-12 Graduation & Scholarships": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/graduation/

Students planning to participate should review the current graduation information and complete all required academic and participation steps by the published deadlines.

Choose the Right International Pathway

Texas Tech K-12 offers two primary diploma pathways for international students.

State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course (EOC) Exams

Students enrolled in Texas Tech High School must pass five STAAR EOC Exams to meet graduation requirements in the following subjects (exceptions may apply):

Step 1: Algebra I

Step 2: English I (Reading/Writing)

Step 3: English II (Reading/Writing)

Step 4: Biology

Step 5: U.S. History

Required 2026-2027 State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness End of Course Testing Dates:

Fall EOC (End of Course Exams):

Step 1: November 30, 2026 – December 11, 2026: Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, U.S. History

TELEPAS (Texas English Language Proficiency Assessment System):

Step 1: February 15, 2027 - March 26, 2027

Spring EOC (End of Course Exams):

Step 1: April 5, 2027 -  April 16, 2027: English I, English II

Step 2: April 12, 2027 - April 23, 2027: Biology, U.S. History

Step 3: April 19, 2027 - April 30, 2027: Algebra I

Spring STAAR (State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness):

Step 1: April 5, 2027 - April 16, 2027: Grades 3-8 Reading Language Arts

Step 2: April 12, 2027 - April 23, 2027: Grade 5 Science, Grade 8 Science, Grade 8 Social Studies

Step 3: April 19, 2027 - April 30, 2027: Grades 3-8 Mathematics

Summer EOC (End of Course Exams):

Step 1: June 14, 2027 -  June 25, 2027: Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, U.S. History

Released test questions can be found on the Texas Education Agency website at this link: Test Questions (Opens in a new tab).

Link for "Test Questions (Opens in a new tab).": https://tea.texas.gov/data-reports/staar/staar-released-test-questions

Foundation Graduation Plan plus Endorsements

If you enrolled in ninth grade during or after the 2014-15 school year, you will graduate under the rules of House Bill 5 (HB 5). HB 5 graduation plans consist of a Foundation Graduation Plan plus one of five endorsements from which students may choose.

Weighted Coursework

Eligible Advanced Placement (AP), Honors, International Baccalaureate (IB) and Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit courses receive additional GPA weight in accordance with Texas Tech K-12 policy.

Eligible transferred coursework with an approved weighted-course designation may also receive the corresponding GPA weight when applied toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

Transfer Grades for the High School Program

Students transferring to Texas Tech High School from an accredited public or private school must provide an official transcript, report card or other required academic records for evaluation.

Texas Tech K-12 will review eligible coursework to determine which credits may be applied toward the student’s Texas Tech High School graduation requirements. Transfer grades from accredited schools are included in the student’s GPA unless the course is designated as local credit or graded on a pass/fail basis.

Students transferring from a homeschool program or non-accredited school or program must provide appropriate academic documentation, such as transcripts or grade reports, for review. Grades from homeschool or non-accredited programs are not directly transferable for credit. Students may earn applicable credit by completing the appropriate CBE or by enrolling in the corresponding course.

Texas Tech K-12 reserves the right to make the final determination regarding the acceptance and application of transferred coursework toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

The following designations will receive weighted credits:

Step 1: Advanced Placement (AP) or Passing (P)

Step 2: Honors

Step 3: International Baccalaureate (IB)

Step 4: Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit

All accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses taken by a student that apply to graduation will be used to compute the Grade Point Average, excluding any approved Physical Education Substitution (SUBPRO) credits and local credit courses.

Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will make every effort to assist students in transferring grades and credits from accredited public or private schools as allowed by Texas Education Agency (TEA) policies and Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS). An official transcript or report card will be required for credit transfer.

Public or Private School Transfer Grades Conversion to Texas Tech K-12 | Public or Private School Transfer Grades Conversion to Texas Tech K-12

A Texas High School Diploma From Anywhere in the World

The Single Diploma pathway is designed for students who want to complete their high school education through Texas Tech K-12.

Students complete Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online coursework and work toward earning a Texas high school diploma.

This pathway may be a good fit for students who:

Step 1: Want a fully online high school experience

Step 2: Want to earn a Texas high school diploma

Step 3: Need flexibility for when and where they learn

Step 4: Have strong English language skills

Step 5: Are prepared for rigorous reading, writing and communication in English

Because coursework is completed in English, strong English proficiency is important for student success.

Endorsements

Please contact a Texas Tech K-12 senior academic advisor via our Support Portal (opens in new tab) for information on graduation plans. For additional graduation requirements, refer to the section on State and National Assessments (opens in a new tab).

Link for "Support Portal (opens in new tab)": https://www.support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb

Link for "State and National Assessments (opens in a new tab).": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/handbook.php#assessments

**Texas Tech K-12 Graduation Path**

- Texas Tech K-12 follows the **Foundation Graduation Plan with Endorsement** as required by the Texas Education Agency (TEA) for students who enrolled in ninth grade during or after the 2014-15 school year.
- This plan includes the Foundation Graduation Plan plus at least one endorsement, allowing students to customize their education based on career interests.
- All students graduating from Texas Tech High School on this plan will also earn the **Distinguished Level of Achievement**, which qualifies them for automatic admission to Texas public universities (Top 10% rule).

**Endorsement Options Available:**
- Arts & Humanities
- Business & Industry
- Multidisciplinary Studies
- STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math)
- Public Services

**Credit Requirements (Foundation Graduation Plan with Endorsement):**
- English: 4 credits
- Math: 4 credits
- Science: 4 credits
- Social Studies: 3 credits
- Foreign Language: 2 credits
- Fine Arts: 1 credit
- Physical Education: 1 credit
- Electives: 7 credits

**Additional Requirements:**
- Pass five State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) End of Course (EOC) exams: Algebra I, Biology, English I, English II, and U.S. History.

**More Information:**
- For a detailed checklist and endorsement options, see the [Personal Graduation Plan Checklist (opens in new tab)](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/pdf/personal-graduation-plan-checklist.pdf).
- For official TEA graduation requirements, visit the [TEA Graduation Toolkit (opens in new tab)](https://tea.texas.gov/about-tea/news-and-multimedia/brochures/tea-brochures).

**Next Step:**  
Contact your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor for personalized guidance on selecting an endorsement and ensuring you meet all graduation requirements.

answer.text:
**FERPA for 18-Year-Old Students at Texas Tech K-12**

When a student turns 18, rights under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) transfer from the parent/guardian to the student. At Texas Tech K-12, FERPA-related requests and permissions are managed through the student’s portal account.

**How to Complete FERPA-Related Actions:**
- **Student Portal:** The 18-year-old student should log in to their Texas Tech K-12 Focus Portal account to manage their educational records and privacy settings.
- **Authorized Users:** To grant access to parents or others, the student can add authorized users/contacts in the portal under the Address & Contacts section.
- **Forms:** Any specific FERPA release forms or requests can be submitted through the Forms tab in the Focus Portal.

**If you need assistance:**
- Contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877
- Email: ttuk12@ttu.edu

**Next Step:**  
Log in to the Focus Portal to manage FERPA permissions or contact Texas Tech K-12 support for further guidance.

**How to Link Your Parent Portal Account to Your Student’s Account**

To connect your Parent Portal account to your student’s account in Texas Tech K-12, follow these steps:

**If You Already Have a Parent Portal Account:**
- Click on "I have an Account Registered on the Parent Portal but would like to Add a Child" (opens in new tab):  
  [Add a Child to Parent Portal](https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/auth/)
- Enter your student’s ID and date of birth to connect them to your account.
- Once entered, your student’s name should appear under "Students."

**If You Do Not Have a Parent Portal Account:**
- Visit the Parent Portal Registration page:  
  [Parent Portal Registration](https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/auth/)
- Follow the prompts to create your account. You will need a unique email address (not shared with your student).
- During registration, you’ll be asked for your student’s matriculation number and date of birth to link the accounts.

**If You Have Trouble Linking Accounts:**
If you are unable to connect your student account to your parent account via the Parent Portal, contact the Texas Tech K-12 office at 1-800-692-6877. Be prepared to verify at least three of the following details:
- Student’s Focus Username
- Student’s Email Address
- Mailing or Physical Address
- Type of Enrollment (Full-time/Part-time)
- External/Former School
- Name of Course Currently Enrolled
- Student Phone Number
- Student ID Number

**Next Step:**
If you need further assistance, please call 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

Identification Cards and Verification of Enrollment (VOE)

As a full-time student, you are eligible to receive a Texas Tech K-12 student identification card and Verification of Attendance (VOE).

Verification of Attendance

If you are a full-time student who wishes to receive a VOE for any purpose, including a driver’s permit, Social Security benefits or child support, avoiding truancy in your local district, or legal documentation of enrollment in a Texas Tech K-12 full-time program, you MUST meet the full-time student eligibility requirements as outlined above.

You may request a Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) VOE Form or an official letter verifying enrollment and attendance from your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. Texas Tech K-12 administration may deny VOE to any student who has not maintained adequate progress to stay on grade level. Request a VOE by emailing a request to your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor. The advisor will require at least two working days for progress review.

If you are denied a VOE, your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor will work with you to outline a progress intervention plan to meet the requirements necessary to receive a VOE in the future.
